name: An inferred physician's household (south division)
head: inf_physician_south_01

arrival.note: NOT AN ARRIVAL, A BOUND. Nothing dates a hypothesised household, and a year would be a claim nobody made. `not_later_than` the scene date states the only thing the inference carries: the town's need is measured on 1 July 1835, so the household is posited as being here by then and at no stated time before it.

party_size_on_arrival.note: Not claimed. The layer infers households, not families: the person entries here are the ones the trade argument requires and nothing counts wives or children, because counting them would multiply a hypothesis by an invention.

origin.note: Not claimed. Where a hypothesised resident came from is unknowable by construction, and the documented layer's origins (Vermont, Washington, Ann Arbor) are evidence about those men and not a distribution to sample from.

reason_for_coming.note: Not claimed for the person. The reason the HOUSEHOLD is in the dataset is the trade argument in research_note, which is a statement about the town and not about a motive.

lives_at.note: THE HOUSEHOLD IS HOUSED, WHICH IS THE POINT OF THE LAYER. recon_1835_south_d7_035 is an anonymous inferred roof already standing on the plat, adopted rather than duplicated: its existence, position and footprint stay conjectural and the adoption adds only the occupant argument. Which roof of the right family and district a hypothesised household occupies is not evidence about that roof; the household needed a dwelling and the programme assigned it one.

works_at.note: physicians_office is a structure record this parcel raises for the purpose, because no roof of the right family stood free in this district. The workplace is assigned from the reconstruction schedule's workshop and store families for this trade.

present_on_scene_date.note: Presence on the scene date IS the hypothesis: this household exists in the dataset because the town of 1 July 1835 demonstrably needed households of this trade. It is not a finding about anybody's whereabouts.

persons.name: A physician (inferred resident, unnamed)

occupation.note: EIGHT PHYSICIANS ARE DOCUMENTED IN THE 1833 TOWN AND THIS DATASET HELD NOT ONE DOCTOR'S OFFICE. Four are written as households in the documented layer. One further physician household is inferred to occupy the office this parcel builds, because naming that office for a documented doctor would attach a real man to an invented building.

persons.note: HYPOTHESISED, AND NOT A PERSON. No source names this resident and none is claimed to: the record asserts that a town of 3,265 people in 398 dwellings held at least this many households of this trade, and asserts nothing whatever about any individual. The name field carries a designation because inventing a surname would make this record indistinguishable at a glance from the documented layer beside it. No figure is drawn (docs/LIBERTIES.md L1). research_note: INFERRED HOUSEHOLD - first of 1 physician households in this layer, in the south division. EIGHT PHYSICIANS ARE DOCUMENTED IN THE 1833 TOWN AND THIS DATASET HELD NOT ONE DOCTOR'S OFFICE. Four are written as households in the documented layer. One further physician household is inferred to occupy the office this parcel builds, because naming that office for a documented doctor would attach a real man to an invented building. METHOD: the count comes from the occupation census in data/reconstruction/1835_inferred_household_programme.json, which calibrates every trade against three things this project already holds - the 1835 town census (3,265 people, 398 dwellings), Andreas's roster of the fall of 1833 (about fifty named people, most with a trade, in a settlement of some 350), and the reconstruction specification's roof schedule, whose workshop and store family targets are treated as the ceiling on a trade rather than as its measure. Every count is stated NET of the documented layer: this dataset infers a tradesman only where it cannot name one.
